transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. For the past 10 months, I've been experiencing this overwhelming surge of energy and staying extremely active all the time. I barely need any sleep at all, sometimes just a few hours a night, but I still feel completely refreshed and ready to go.
During these periods of high energy and reduced sleep, have you ever had thoughts that others might not understand, like believing you have special powers or that people are watching you?

Yes, absolutely, but it only happens when I'm in these high-energy phases. I get this strong belief that I have special powers and unique abilities, while at the same time feeling like I'm being watched or monitored by others. Once my energy levels drop and I start sleeping again, those thoughts completely go away.

No, they completely stop. When I'm not in those high-energy phases, I don't hear anything or feel paranoid at all, and everything goes back to normal.

inference_history.note: The patient describes a prolonged period of increased energy, hyperactivity, and significantly reduced need for sleep with no impairment in functioning—core symptoms of a manic episode. This strongly suggests a bipolar-related disorder. The duration (10 months) is unusually long for a typical manic episode, which usually lasts at least one week, but this may indicate an extended manic phase or chronic course. Given the presence of manic symptoms, the primary differential includes Bipolar I Disorder. Psychotic features cannot be ruled out without further assessment, hence Bipolar I with Psychotic Features is included. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type) remains a possibility if there are prominent psychotic symptoms occurring outside mood episodes, but currently there is insufficient evidence to confirm this. No depressive or psychotic symptoms have been reported yet, so other disorders such as Major Depressive Disorder or schizophrenia spectrum disorders are less likely at this stage.
